C05-M02-L01-F1.title: How much a reconnaissance action touches the target
C05-M02-L01-F1.caption: Reconnaissance actions on a scale from prior knowledge to systematic probing, grouped into passive, low-touch and active bands.
C05-M02-L01-F1.alt: Scale with five ticks from left to right: Prior knowledge (scope document, asset list), Third-party records (DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, CT logs, search engines), Ordinary visit (one request to a public page), Targeted requests (/robots.txt, /admin, candidate paths) and Systematic probing (port scans, name brute-force, service enumeration). A green passive band covers the first two ticks, where no packet reaches the target; an orange low-touch band covers the ordinary visit; a red active band covers targeted requests and systematic probing.

ticks.label: Third-party records
ticks.sub: DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, CT logs, search engines

ticks.label: Ordinary visit
ticks.sub: one request to a public page

bands.label: passive: no packet reaches the target

C05-M02-L01-F1.note: Everything right of the second tick sends traffic to the target and needs authorisation, however gentle it looks.

C05-M02-L01-F2.title: The reconnaissance gate: may this action run?
C05-M02-L01-F2.caption: Every planned reconnaissance action passes three questions before it is executed; ambiguity resolves to stop.
C05-M02-L01-F2.alt: Decision graph. Planned recon action leads to Sends traffic to the target? No leads to Proceed as passive. Yes leads to Asset listed in scope? No leads to Stop: park lead, ask client. Yes leads to Activity, time and rate permitted? No leads to Stop: park lead, ask client. Yes leads to Proceed and log.
C05-M02-L01-F2.note: There is no "probably in scope" branch: ambiguity resolves to no.
